question: Could you tell me the number of orders, average payment per order and customer lifespan in weeks of the 3 custumers with the highest average payment per order, where the lifespan is calculated by subtracting the earliest purchase date from the latest purchase date in days, dividing by seven, and if the result is less than seven days, setting it to 1.0?
sql:
-- Every customer has exactly 1 order, so all lifespan_weeks will be 1.0 (since same day = 0 days diff, 0/7 < 1, so 1.0)
-- The top 3 customers by avg_payment_per_order are already identified.
-- Now let me build the final query with both customer_id and customer_unique_id as requested in the guidelines

WITH customer_order_payments AS (
    SELECT 
        o.customer_id,
        o.order_id,
        o.order_purchase_timestamp,
        COALESCE(SUM(op.payment_value), 0) AS total_payment_for_order
    FROM orders o
    LEFT JOIN order_payments op ON o.order_id = op.order_id
    GROUP BY o.customer_id, o.order_id, o.order_purchase_timestamp
),
customer_stats AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_id,
        COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS num_orders,
        SUM(total_payment_for_order) AS total_payment,
        SUM(total_payment_for_order) * 1.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS avg_payment_per_order,
        MIN(CAST(order_purchase_timestamp AS TIMESTAMP)) AS earliest_purchase,
        MAX(CAST(order_purchase_timestamp AS TIMESTAMP)) AS latest_purchase
    FROM customer_order_payments
    GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT 
    cs.customer_id,
    c.customer_unique_id,
    cs.num_orders,
    cs.avg_payment_per_order,
    CASE 
        WHEN (CAST(cs.latest_purchase AS DATE) - CAST(cs.earliest_purchase AS DATE)) / 7.0 < 1.0 THEN 1.0
        ELSE (CAST(cs.latest_purchase AS DATE) - CAST(cs.earliest_purchase AS DATE)) / 7.0
    END AS lifespan_weeks
FROM customer_stats cs
JOIN customers c ON cs.customer_id = c.customer_id
ORDER BY cs.avg_payment_per_order DESC
LIMIT 3

The core transactional tables are orders, order_items, order_payments, and order_reviews. Orders links to customers via customer_id and to order_items via order_id. Order_items connects to products through product_id and to sellers via seller_id. Order_payments also joins to orders using order_id. Product category names in products link to translations in product_category_name_translation via product_category_name. function.arguments:
{"sql": "
-- Step 1: Understand the data - get customer order counts, total payments, and average payment per order
-- Join orders with order_payments to get payment info per order per customer
WITH customer_order_payments AS (
    SELECT 
        o.customer_id,
        o.order_id,
        SUM(op.payment_value) AS total_payment_for_order
    FROM orders o
    LEFT JOIN order_payments op ON o.order_id = op.order_id
    GROUP BY o.customer_id, o.order_id
),
customer_stats AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_id,
        COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS num_orders,
        SUM(total_payment_for_order) AS total_payment,
        SUM(total_payment_for_order) * 1.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS avg_payment_per_order,
        MIN(CAST(order_purchase_timestamp AS TIMESTAMP)) AS earliest_purchase,
        MAX(CAST(order_purchase_timestamp AS TIMESTAMP)) AS latest_purchase
    FROM customer_order_payments
    GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT 
    customer_id,
    num_orders,
    total_payment,
    avg_payment_per_order,
    earliest_purchase,
    latest_purchase,
    (CAST(latest_purchase AS DATE) - CAST(earliest_purchase AS DATE)) AS days_between,
    CASE 
        WHEN (CAST(latest_purchase AS DATE) - CAST(earliest_purchase AS DATE)) / 7.0 < 1.0 THEN 1.0
        ELSE (CAST(latest_purchase AS DATE) - CAST(earliest_purchase AS DATE)) / 7.0
    END AS lifespan_weeks
FROM customer_stats
ORDER BY avg_payment_per_order DESC
LIMIT 10
"}

-- Let me verify the lifespan calculation. The question says:
-- "lifespan is calculated by subtracting the earliest purchase date from the latest purchase date in days, 
-- dividing by seven, and if the result is less than seven days, setting it to 1.0"
-- So the logic is: days_diff / 7.0, if < 1.0 then 1.0

-- Let me also verify the date subtraction works correctly in DuckDB
-- In DuckDB, DATE - DATE gives an integer of days

SELECT 
    customer_id,
    CAST(earliest_purchase AS DATE) AS earliest_date,
    CAST(latest_purchase AS DATE) AS latest_date,
    CAST(latest_purchase AS DATE) - CAST(earliest_purchase AS DATE) AS days_diff,
    (CAST(latest_purchase AS DATE) - CAST(earliest_purchase AS DATE)) / 7.0 AS weeks_raw,
    CASE 
        WHEN (CAST(latest_purchase AS DATE) - CAST(earliest_purchase AS DATE)) / 7.0 < 1.0 THEN 1.0
        ELSE (CAST(latest_purchase AS DATE) - CAST(earliest_purchase AS DATE)) / 7.0
    END AS lifespan_weeks
FROM (
    SELECT 
        o.customer_id,
        MIN(CAST(o.order_purchase_timestamp AS TIMESTAMP)) AS earliest_purchase,
        MAX(CAST(o.order_purchase_timestamp AS TIMESTAMP)) AS latest_purchase
    FROM orders o
    GROUP BY o.customer_id
    LIMIT 3
)
"}
